summary: Dedicated (us-east) sustained throughput below committed floor for Vidorama deployment
description:
Issue summary
- Customer (Vidorama) reports sustained throughput below their Dedicated committed floor in us-east.
- Symptoms observed over multiple hours (not a transient warmup dip).

Customer impact
- Production inference throughput ~25–35% below expected; customer reports request queueing and elevated end-user latency.
- Customer states they are operating within agreed model/version + context constraints and not exceeding their committed concurrency guidance.

Environment
- Deployment: ded-vidorama-ue1-17 (Dedicated)
- Region: us-east
- Route: /v1/chat/completions (streaming enabled)
- Model pinned: llama-3.1-70b-instruct
- Workload shape (per customer): steady-state concurrency 24–40; input ~600–1,000 tokens; output ~150–300 tokens

Expected vs observed
- Expected: meet or exceed committed throughput floor (per Dedicated order form; customer quoting “committed tokens/sec”) during steady state after warmup.
- Observed: throughput plateauing around ~5.5k–6.2k tok/s (aggregate deployment output tokens/sec) for extended windows; intermittent dips to ~4.8k tok/s.

Time window (customer)
- First noticed: 2025-02-26 ~18:00 UTC
- Reported to Support: 2025-02-27 09:12 UTC

Initial triage notes
- Confirmed this is Dedicated deployment traffic (not Hosted) and model is pinned.
- No evidence of customer-side throttling (429s) in gateway logs for the timeframe.
- Preliminary SLO panel indicates elevated burn rate for throughput floor on this deployment.

Dashboards / evidence
- Dedicated Throughput SLO dashboard (internal): panel “Throughput vs Floor (deployment_id=ded-vidorama-ue1-17)” shows sustained under-floor windows.
- Saturation signals: GPU utilization high, queue depth elevated, batcher frequently at max batch tokens, increased prefill time.
- Fleet view showed deployment running with fewer healthy workers than expected for its reserved shape.

Hypothesis (most likely)
- Effective capacity reduction in the dedicated pool (one worker node out / GPU unavailable) causing sustained throughput drop.

Mitigation performed
- Infra migrated the deployment to a healthy reserved pool matching the contracted shape in us-east and restored expected worker count.
- Performed controlled runtime restart to clear degraded worker assignments and rebuild warm caches.
- Monitored for 60 minutes post-migration; throughput stabilized above floor.

Customer communication
- Acknowledged incident, provided ongoing updates during migration window, and requested customer validation after recovery.

Resolution
- Root cause: dedicated pool drift (degraded worker capacity) after an automatic node drain + failed replacement, leaving the deployment under-provisioned for ~14 hours.
- Recovery: moved deployment to spare capacity; replacement fix queued with Fleet.

Follow-ups
- Add/enable alerting on “provisioned worker count < expected for tier/shape” for Dedicated deployments.
- Review change management around node drains for Dedicated pools in us-east; ensure spare capacity availability or proactive customer notice.
comments: 2025-02-27 09:18 UTC — Dev Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Confirming details: deployment_id, model pin, approx concurrency + input/output tokens, and whether requests are streaming. Also requesting 3–5 request_ids during the slow windows for correlation.

2025-02-27 09:33 UTC — Customer (Vidorama): Provided deployment_id=ded-vidorama-ue1-17. Streaming enabled. Concurrency ~30. Input ~800 tokens, output ~200 tokens. Slow since yesterday ~18:00 UTC. Provided request IDs: req_7d2a… / req_91bf… / req_3a0c…

2025-02-27 10:02 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support Eng): Correlated request_ids in logs; no elevated 5xx. Gateway latency increases appear downstream (time to first token + overall stream duration). No 429s from customer org. Escalating to SRE/Infra with deployment_id + timeframe.

2025-02-27 10:20 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE): Checked Dedicated Throughput SLO dashboard: throughput below floor for multiple 5-min windows; burn-rate alert would have triggered at current thresholds. Saturation looks like fewer active workers than expected. Suspect pool drift / worker loss vs pure workload variance.

2025-02-27 10:41 UTC — Irene Choi (Infra): Fleet view shows ded-vidorama-ue1-17 assigned 6/8 workers healthy (2 in drain/failed replacement state). Likely related to overnight host maintenance event. Working with Fleet to either replace nodes or migrate deployment to spare pool.

2025-02-27 11:05 UTC — Vanessa Ortiz (Fleet): Confirmed: node drain occurred; replacement request stuck due to capacity reservation mis-match in us-east A100 pool. We have spare capacity in alternate dedicated pool; recommend migration to restore 8/8 now, then fix reservation accounting to prevent recurrence.

2025-02-28 02:12 UTC — Irene Choi (Infra): Executing migration of ded-vidorama-ue1-17 to healthy pool (us-east). ETA 10–15 minutes. Expect brief connection churn; routing will drain old workers before cutover.

2025-02-28 02:31 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support Eng): Migration complete. Observing throughput rising to ~8.6k–9.1k tok/s (output) and queue depth returning to baseline. Asking customer to validate from their side.
2025-02-28 03:10 UTC — Customer (Vidorama): Confirmed throughput back to expected and backlog cleared. Streaming responsiveness improved. Thanks.

2025-03-03 16:40 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support Eng): Closing loop. Root cause: under-provisioned worker count due to drain + failed replacement in us-east dedicated pool; mitigated by pool migration. Follow-ups filed with Infra/SRE to add worker-count drift alerting and tighten drain safeguards for Dedicated pools.
